examples.en: I am barely getting by on my salary.
The shop has no customers, so it is barely hanging on.
I scraped together my tuition with part-time jobs.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 적자 속에서도 근근이 문을 열고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is barely staying open despite running at a loss.

examples.ko: 근근이 모은 돈을 병원비로 다 썼어요.
examples.en: I spent all the money I had barely saved up on hospital bills.

examples.ko: 할머니는 작은 밭에서 나온 것으로 근근이 먹고 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother barely got by on what came from her small field.

explain: '겨우', '간신히'와 비슷하지만 '근근이'는 어려운 형편에서 힘들게 이어 가는 모습에 많이 써요. '살다, 버티다, 모으다, 이어 가다'와 잘 어울려요. '합격선을 근근이 넘다'처럼 한 번에 아슬아슬하게 해내는 일에는 '간신히'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '겨우' and '간신히', but '근근이' leans toward continuing with difficulty in hard circumstances. It goes well with '살다', '버티다', '모으다' and '이어 가다'. For barely pulling off a single thing, like just clearing a passing score, '간신히' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The market the day before a holiday is as chaotic as a bazaar.
On the first day of the sale, the store turned into a zoo.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 많아서 역 앞이 도떼기시장 같았어요.
examples.en: There were so many people that the area in front of the station was a madhouse.
During breaks, the classroom turns into a madhouse.

examples.ko: 도떼기시장에서 물건을 사려면 큰 소리로 말해야 해요.
examples.en: To buy things in a chaotic market, you have to speak loudly.
Yesterday's event hall was a madhouse, so I was overwhelmed.

explain: 사람이 많고 시끄러워서 정신없는 장소나 상황을 시장에 빗대어 말해요. 시장 자체보다 행사장, 교실, 매장 같은 곳에 비유로 쓸 때가 많아요. 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It compares a crowded, noisy, chaotic place or situation to a market. It is often used figuratively for event halls, classrooms or stores rather than markets themselves. It carries a slightly negative tone.

examples.en: I never got back the money I lent my friend.
My wages weren't paid, so life is really hard.

examples.ko: 외상값을 떼이지 않으려면 계약서를 써야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid not getting paid, you should write a contract.

examples.ko: 돈을 떼인 사람들이 사무실 앞에 모였어요.
examples.en: People who were never paid gathered in front of the office.

examples.ko: 보증금을 떼일까 봐 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep for fear of losing my deposit.

examples.ko: 한 번 떼이고 나니까 이제 돈은 안 빌려줘요.
examples.en: After getting burned once, I don't lend money anymore.

explain: 받을 돈을 못 받았을 때 피해 본 사람이 쓰는 말이에요. 돈을 안 주는 쪽은 '떼먹다'를 쓰고, 보통 '돈을 떼이다'로 말해요.
explain_en: This is what the victim says when they can't collect money owed to them. The person who doesn't pay is described with '떼먹다', and the usual phrase is '돈을 떼이다'.

examples.en: At the typhoon news, people stockpiled ramyeon.
The supermarket has no toilet paper because of panic buying.
Panic buying harms other people.

examples.ko: 물건이 부족해질까 봐 사재기하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people hoard because they fear a shortage.

examples.ko: 가격이 오르기 전에 사재기에 나선 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: Some people started stockpiling before prices rose.
Don't hoard; buy only what you need.

explain: 필요 이상으로 많이 사서 쌓아 두는 것이라 보통 좋지 않은 느낌으로 말해요. 뉴스에서는 태풍, 가격 인상, 물건 부족 같은 상황에서 자주 나와요. 동사로는 '사재기하다'라고 써요.
explain_en: It means buying far more than you need and piling it up, so it carries a negative tone. In the news it appears often with typhoons, price hikes and shortages. The verb form is '사재기하다'.

en: person with no property at all; penniless person

examples.en: His business failed and he became penniless overnight.
He came up to Seoul with absolutely nothing.
I almost lost everything because of stocks.
Once I was left penniless, my friends disappeared too.
Before payday I'm practically broke.

examples.ko: 잘못된 투자로 재산을 날려 알거지가 된 사람 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a man who lost his fortune in a bad investment and ended up penniless.

explain: 가진 것이 하나도 없는 사람을 말해요. '빈털터리'와 비슷하지만 '거지'가 들어가서 더 센 표현이에요. 월급날 전에 '나 알거지야'처럼 과장해서 농담으로도 써요.
explain_en: It means a person with absolutely nothing. It is similar to '빈털터리' but stronger because it contains '거지' (beggar). People also joke with it, saying '나 알거지야' before payday.

en: be stagnant; be stalled; (traffic) be congested

examples.en: The roads get congested at rush hour.

examples.ko: 우리 회사의 성장이 몇 년째 정체되었어요.
examples.en: Our company's growth has been stagnant for years.
The traffic jam lasted so long that I was very late.
Exports have been stagnant for months, so I am worried.
I want to change the stagnant mood.
Cars are backed up because of the snow.

explain: 길이 막힐 때는 '막히다'가 더 일상적이고, '정체되다'는 뉴스의 교통 정보에서 자주 나와요. 일이나 경제가 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때도 써요. 반대로 빠르게 나아갈 때는 '성장하다', '발전하다'를 써요.
explain_en: For roads, '막히다' is more everyday, and '정체되다' appears often in news traffic reports. It also describes work or the economy that is not moving forward. When things move ahead quickly, you say '성장하다' or '발전하다'.

p.n: Grammatical either way, but 정체되다 sounds more natural for traffic.
